identity_snapshot.short_description: A restoration civilization grown from a living root-and-memory network, built on healing sap, seasonal cycles, communal groves, and the conviction that wounds must be cleansed rather than commanded.
identity_snapshot.civilization_type: Decentralized council of grove-communities bound by a living root network and elder consensus.
identity_snapshot.core_belief: Life moves in cycles; a wound healed restores the whole, but a wound used becomes the wound.
primary_corruption_risk: Sacrificing the few groves to save the many
identity_snapshot.domain_stone_or_source: The Heartroot Loom — an ancient living network of root-and-memory anchored to the Verdance Stone fragment.
identity_snapshot.magic_style: Sap weaving and root communion; growth, healing, and tree-memory drawn from the living network.
identity_snapshot.main_magic_cost: A life-tithe paid back into the cycle, and memory given to the tree-network.
identity_snapshot.political_center: The Circle of Elders convened at the Heartroot grove.
identity_snapshot.military_identity: Patient defenders: entangle, endure, and outlast rather than conquer.
identity_snapshot.economic_base: Healing sap, grove-grown medicine, seed commons, and timber stewardship.
identity_snapshot.biggest_internal_conflict: Whether survival ever justifies wielding corrupted sap as a weapon (Hollow Pact) versus cleansing it slowly at great cost (Rootwarden Conservators).
identity_snapshot.biggest_external_threat: Abyss soul-harvest in the border villages, draining the root network of names and memory.
identity_snapshot.keeper_exploit: The Keeper makes Verdance defend itself by becoming the rot it fears, so its resistance damages its own soul-flow from within.
identity_snapshot.void_lie: If rot saved them, why call it corruption?

canon_facts: Verdance is bound by the Heartroot Loom, a living root-and-memory network tied to a fragment of the fractured pure Nexus Stone.
Healing sap is Verdance's sacred resource and chief export; corrupted sap is its sacred wound.
The Circle of Elders governs by consensus; no single ruler commands Verdance.
Rootwell sites are places where the network's memory pools; corrupted rootwells whisper stolen names.
Rootwarden Conservators guard the cycle; the Hollow Pact weaponizes corruption; the Sap Commons distribute healing.
Communion Grovekeepers read tree-memory and arbitrate sacred judgments through the network.
cannot_contradict: Verdance magic must always involve the cycle, consent, restoration, or living memory — never sterile command.
Verdance corruption must distort restoration into rot-mastery and patience into stagnation, never become generic darkness.
Verdance internal politics must respect the Rootwarden / Hollow Pact / Sap Commons / Communion fracture.
Corrupted sap can grant real power, but using it always deepens the soul-flow wound it came from.

metaphysical_role.principle_embodied: Restoration and cycle — the return of damaged life to wholeness through patient renewal.
metaphysical_role.nexus_stone_aspect: The Stone's capacity to hold and re-weave memory, letting identity persist through death, decay, and regrowth.
metaphysical_role.soul_flow_shaped: Verdance lets the dead and their names rejoin the network as living memory, feeding the next season's growth.
metaphysical_role.natural_magic: Sap weaving and root communion: healing, growth, and memory drawn from the living network.
metaphysical_role.when_extreme: Restoration calcifies into stagnation, or inverts into mastery of rot — the wound used instead of healed.
metaphysical_role.keeper_exploits_extremity: The Keeper tempts Verdance to command corruption to survive, turning its restorative network into a conduit for the rot.

domain_stone.origin: Grown over millennia from the first grove planted upon a fragment of the fractured pure Nexus Stone, now a continent-spanning weave of root and memory.
domain_stone.public_knowledge: The Loom remembers every grove and carries messages root to root; it heals what is patiently tended.
domain_stone.hidden_truth: Abyss soul-harvest and corrupted rootwells are tearing names out of the weave faster than the cycle can re-grow them; whole memory-strands are going silent.
failure_symptoms: Roots whisper stolen names at night
Healing sap curdles to corrupted sap
healing_methods: Communion judgment to re-weave broken strands
domain_stone.keeper_attack_vector: Spread corrupted rootwells so Verdance must either let villages die or wield the rot, both of which feed the wound.
domain_stone.void_attack_vector: Offer the corrupted sap's power now in exchange for a strand of memory torn from the weave later.

soul_flow.healthy_soul_flow_description: The dead and their names rejoin the Heartroot Loom as living memory, nourishing the next cycle of growth.
soul_flow.damaged_soul_flow_description: Names are torn from the weave and trapped in corrupted rootwells, where the rot speaks through stolen identities.
forbidden_soul_processes: Commanding corrupted sap to bind the living
Forcing a grove's memory open without consent
healing_methods: Returning erased names to the weave
factions_that_disrupt_soul_flow: Abyss Ash Ledger agents on the border
soul_flow.keeper_disruption_strategy: Multiply corrupted rootwells until the weave forgets more than it remembers.
soul_flow.void_disruption_strategy: Whisper that the rot is just another season, so the grieving stop cleansing and start commanding it.

true_virtues.name: Restoration
true_virtues.healthy_definition: The patient return of damaged life and memory to wholeness, rather than its replacement or removal.
true_virtues.cultural_expression: Communities mend rather than discard; even a corrupted grove is a patient to be healed.
true_virtues.heroic_expression: A defender cleanses a wound at personal cost rather than burning or commanding it.
true_virtues.political_expression: Elders are judged by what they restore, not what they conquer.
true_virtues.magical_expression: Sap weaving heals and regrows; its power scales with the caster's tithe to the cycle.
true_virtues.economic_expression: Healing sap is a commons to be shared, not a monopoly to be hoarded.
true_virtues.military_expression: Victory is denying the enemy the ground without poisoning it.
true_virtues.common_saying: Tend the wound, do not wear it.

true_virtues.name: Communion
true_virtues.healthy_definition: The conviction that no grove is alone; memory, judgment, and grief are shared through the living weave.
true_virtues.cultural_expression: Decisions are reached by consensus carried root to root.
true_virtues.heroic_expression: A hero submits a hard choice to communion rather than acting alone.
true_virtues.political_expression: Authority flows from the network's consensus, not personal command.
true_virtues.magical_expression: Root communion lets distant groves share memory, warning, and counsel.
true_virtues.economic_expression: Surpluses are pooled in seed and sap commons.
true_virtues.military_expression: Warnings travel the roots faster than any courier.
true_virtues.common_saying: One root feels what the whole forest fears.

true_virtues.name: Stewardship
true_virtues.healthy_definition: Responsibility for the cycle across generations — taking only what regrows and leaving the weave whole.
true_virtues.cultural_expression: Each grove keeps a ledger of what it owes the next season.
true_virtues.heroic_expression: A steward sacrifices a short-term win to protect a long-term cycle.
true_virtues.political_expression: Leaders who exhaust a grove for gain are shamed and replaced.
true_virtues.magical_expression: Sap is drawn at a rate the grove can replenish.
true_virtues.economic_expression: Timber and sap quotas are set by the grove's regrowth, not by demand.
true_virtues.military_expression: Scorched-earth tactics are taboo; the land must survive the war.
true_virtues.common_saying: Borrow from the grove; you cannot inherit from it twice.

corrupted_virtues.corrupted_definition: The belief that corruption can be commanded and aimed rather than cleansed, turning the wound into a weapon.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_begins: A desperate grove survives an attack by weaponizing corrupted sap and is praised for it.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_spreads: Survivor stories, Hollow Pact recruitment among the frightened, and the simple fact that it works.
who_suffers: Future seasons of the poisoned grove
corrupted_virtues.keeper_benefit: Verdance's own resistance becomes a conduit that spreads the rot it fears.
corrupted_virtues.void_lie: If rot saved them, why call it corruption?
visible_symptoms: Corrupted-sap traps left active after battle
corrupted_virtues.late_stage_consequence: Whole grove-communities become dependent on the corruption keeping them alive.

corrupted_virtues.corrupted_definition: Using the network's consensus to bury inconvenient truths and silence dissenting groves.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_begins: Elders suppress a frightening communion-finding to avoid panic.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_spreads: Comfort in conformity, fear of being cut from the weave, and the convenience of one agreed story.
corrupted_virtues.keeper_benefit: Lets corrupted rootwells grow unspoken until they are unstoppable.
corrupted_virtues.void_lie: A united forest cannot afford a frightened branch.
visible_symptoms: Communion findings that never reach the Commons
Groves cut from the weave for dissent
corrupted_virtues.late_stage_consequence: Verdance learns of catastrophes only when they have already spread.

corrupted_virtues.corrupted_definition: Stagnation disguised as patience — refusing necessary action until the cycle decays.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_begins: An elder counsels waiting for the cycle to heal a wound that is actually accelerating.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_spreads: Cultural reverence for patience and fear of fire-like Radiance haste.
who_suffers: Villages waiting for help that never comes
corrupted_virtues.keeper_benefit: Buys the rot the one thing it needs most: time.
corrupted_virtues.void_lie: Haste is how Radiance burns. Wait, and the cycle will provide.
visible_symptoms: Endless deliberation as a wound spreads
Aid arriving a season too late
corrupted_virtues.late_stage_consequence: A healable wound becomes a permanent scar in the weave.

keeper_exploit_pattern.corruption_strategy: Force a choice between letting villages die and wielding the rot, so either way the weave is damaged and Verdance distrusts itself.
preferred_crisis_conditions: A grove cornered with no clean option
keeper_exploit_pattern.domain_stone_damage_type: Strands torn from the Heartroot Loom faster than the cycle can regrow them.
keeper_exploit_pattern.common_lie: The rot is just another season; learn to ride it.
keeper_exploit_pattern.long_term_goal: Turn the living restorative network into a conduit for corruption, cracking the prison from inside Verdance's own roots.

void_temptation_pattern.temptation_phrase: If rot saved them, why call it corruption?
void_temptation_pattern.immediate_benefit: Corrupted sap grants potent, instant growth or lethal entangling traps without the slow tithe to the cycle.
void_temptation_pattern.hidden_cost: Each use deepens the rootwell wound it came from and binds a strand of the user's memory to the rot.
void_temptation_pattern.identity_damage: The user begins to think in the rot's logic, mistaking mastery of the wound for healing it.
void_temptation_pattern.soul_flow_damage: Names near the use point are loosened from the weave and pooled in the corrupted rootwell.
void_temptation_pattern.reality_damage: Soil and season warp locally; plants grow wrong and out of time.
visible_stage_1_symptoms: Sap with a faint dark sheen
visible_stage_2_symptoms: The user hears the rootwell at night
visible_stage_3_symptoms: A corrupted rootwell speaks the user's own name
Whole groves dependent on the rot
Children dreaming the rot's stolen memories

magic_systems.source: Living sap drawn from the Heartroot Loom and tithed back into the cycle.
abuse_modes: Drawing sap faster than a grove regrows
magic_systems.keeper_corruption_vector: Reframe corrupted sap as a faster, stronger weave.
magic_systems.void_enhancement_vector: Offer corrupted-sap potency without the tithe, deferring the cost into the weave.

magic_systems.source: The Heartroot Loom's memory-strands, read and spoken through rootwells.
abuse_modes: Reading a grove's memory without consent
magic_systems.keeper_corruption_vector: Turn consensus into the Silencing Consensus.
magic_systems.void_enhancement_vector: Offer access to harvested names as borrowed power.

magic_costs.description: Sap weaving draws on the weaver's own vitality, repaid into the cycle over the season.
magic_costs.minor_effect: Tiredness and a day's wilting of vigor.
magic_costs.moderate_effect: Seasonal frailty; the weaver must rest within the grove to recover.
magic_costs.severe_effect: Permanent vitality loss, accepted as a gift to the cycle.
magic_costs.recovery_method: Rest within a healthy grove and communal renewal.
magic_costs.permanent_risk: Death, or a hollowness that tempts the weaver toward corrupted shortcuts.

magic_costs.description: Deep root communion requires the speaker to give a memory into the weave.
magic_costs.moderate_effect: Gaps in personal memory that the weave now holds.
magic_costs.severe_effect: Loss of self-defining memories; identity destabilizes.
magic_costs.recovery_method: Retrieving the memory from the weave through patient communion.
magic_costs.permanent_risk: Memory fracture the Keeper can exploit, or a name lost to a corrupted well.

magic_costs.description: Corrupted sap grants potency without the life-tithe, but binds the user to the wound it came from.
magic_costs.minor_effect: A faint dark sheen on the user's weave; unease.
magic_costs.moderate_effect: Soil corruption near the user; the rootwell begins to know them.
magic_costs.severe_effect: The user's name loosens from the weave; the corruption thinks through them.
magic_costs.recovery_method: Cleansing communion, returning to the cycle, and rarely full reversal.
magic_costs.permanent_risk: Identity dissolution into the rot; a corrupted rootwell that speaks the user's name.

government.government_type: Decentralized consensus-confederation of grove-communities bound by the living network.
government.ruling_body: The Circle of Elders, convened at the Heartroot grove.
government.religious_authority: Communion Grovekeepers, who read tree-memory and render sacred judgments.
government.military_authority: The Bramble Thornguard, raised seasonally from the groves.
government.economic_authority: The Sap Commons, which sets sap and seed quotas.
government.magical_authority: Rootwarden Conservators, who certify cleansing and police corrupted-sap use.
government.succession_or_selection_method: Elders are chosen by their grove and confirmed in communion; influence follows restored trust, not heredity.
government.legitimacy_source: Consensus carried through the weave and a record of what one has restored.
known_cracks_in_legitimacy: Consensus too slow for fast-moving rot
Border groves feeling abandoned by the center
Silenced warnings eroding trust in the elders
emergency_powers: Communion lockdown of a wounded rootwell
corruption_vulnerabilities: Hollow Pact infiltration of desperate groves

class_structure.description: Readers of tree-memory and keepers of the weave's sacred judgments.
burdens: Blamed when warnings come too late
class_structure.economic_role: Coordinate the commons through the weave.
common_grievances: Pressured to join the Silencing Consensus

class_structure.description: Healers, farmers, sap-tappers, and grove laborers — the body of Verdance.
privileges: Share in the sap and seed commons
burdens: First to suffer when groves are quarantined or harvested
Pressured toward corrupted shortcuts when cornered

class_structure.description: Guardians of the cycle who cleanse corruption and police rot-wielding.
class_structure.economic_role: Certify which groves are safe to harvest.
common_grievances: Split between cleansing and the Hollow Pact's results
upward_mobility_paths: Successful cleansing of a major rootwell
downward_mobility_risks: Being seen to rely on corruption when afraid

trade_routes: The Sap Road to Sanctuary markets
economy.wartime_economy_behavior: Redirects sap to the wounded and may embargo exports to pressure reckless neighbors, accepting its own scarcity.
famine_or_shortage_risks: Border groves cut off by Abyss raids
exploitative_practices: Hollow Pact selling rot-potency to the desperate
economy.keeper_attack_vector: Engineer a healing-sap famine so Verdance over-harvests or turns to corrupted sap to meet demand.

military_doctrine.strategic_identity: Entangle, endure, and outlast; deny ground without poisoning it.
military_doctrine.defensive_strategy: Layered living barriers, ambush from the brush, and tireless attrition.
military_doctrine.offensive_strategy: Rare and reluctant; reclaim and cleanse rather than conquer.
military_doctrine.logistics_strategy: The root network carries warning and counsel faster than any foe; supply is grown locally.
military_doctrine.intelligence_strategy: Root communion gives unmatched early warning but is blind where the weave is silenced or corrupted.
taboo_tactics: Poisoning a grove to deny it
desperate_tactics: Flooding a valley to drown a threat
Quarantine by burning a strand of the weave
common_weaknesses: Blind where the weave is corrupted
Vulnerable to fire and to patience-as-paralysis
military_doctrine.keeper_exploit: Corner a grove so its only fast option is the rot.
military_doctrine.void_escalation: Offer corrupted-sap traps that win the skirmish and lose the soil.

typical_warfront_goals: Preserve the soil for future seasons
preferred_escalation_methods: Cutting off an enemy's supply through overgrowth
warfront_behavior.negotiation_style: Slow, consensus-bound, and mistrustful of haste; values demonstrated restoration.
betrayal_conditions: A grove is poisoned to win
Harvested names are sold to Abyss
alliance_conditions: A partner who cleanses rather than burns
warfront_behavior.occupation_style: Reclaim-and-heal; risks Frozen Patience leaving wounds half-treated.
warfront_behavior.resistance_style: Endless entangling attrition; the forest itself fights and does not tire.

major_locations.name: The Heartroot Grove
major_locations.location_type: Sacred capital grove and seat of consensus
major_locations.description: The oldest grove, where the Heartroot Loom's strands converge into a living cathedral of root and memory.
major_locations.political_function: Seat of the Circle of Elders and communion judgments.
major_locations.economic_function: Hub of the seed and sap commons.
major_locations.magical_function: Strongest node of the living network; source of deep communion.
major_locations.military_function: Symbolic heart; lightly defended, heavily warded by the weave.
major_locations.spiritual_function: Site of naming-into-the-weave and the recovery of lost names.
major_locations.civilian_function: Pilgrimage grove and gathering place for the consensus.
known_secrets: A silenced communion-finding about an accelerating border wound
major_locations.keeper_attack_vector: Let the Silencing Consensus bury the border warning until the rot reaches the Heartroot.
void_symptoms: A faint wrong note in deep communion
Named seeds occasionally sprouting strangers' memories
quest_hooks: Recover a name the weave has lost

major_locations.name: Thornveil Refuge
major_locations.location_type: Border refuge grove sheltering refugees from the Abyss frontier
major_locations.description: A bramble-walled sanctuary crowded with refugees, shadowed by a corrupted rootwell waking beneath it.
major_locations.economic_function: Strained sap and food distribution point.
major_locations.magical_function: Site of an awakening corrupted rootwell (the Rootwell Awakening clock).
major_locations.military_function: Front line against Abyss raids and Hollow Pact incursion.
major_locations.spiritual_function: Where the weave's wound is most audible; names whispered at night.
major_locations.civilian_function: Home to refugees, healers, and the grieving.
known_secrets: Some wardens quietly tolerate Hollow Pact traps
major_locations.keeper_attack_vector: Corner the refuge so its defenders embrace corrupted-sap traps to survive.
quest_hooks: Cleanse or seal the waking rootwell
Decide whether to expose the wardens tolerating Hollow Pact traps
Recover the erased name buried beneath the root archive

culture.daily_life_summary: Life follows the season and the sap-tide; work is communal, grief is composted into growth, and the weave is always listening.
culture.family_customs: Families plant a named seed for each newborn, linking them to the grove's memory.
culture.love_and_marriage_customs: Couples graft a shared sapling; its health is read as an omen of the bond.
culture.education_system: Children learn the weave's songs and the cycle's lore from naming-keepers before letters.
culture.work_and_apprenticeship: Apprentices learn from a grove-keeper through the seasons; knowledge is shared, not owned.
culture.food_and_market_life: Sap-teas, grove fruit, and grown breads; markets trade in seeds, medicine, and memory-tokens.
culture.funeral_or_death_customs: The dead are named into the weave and their seed planted, so their memory feeds the next season.
public_honors: A name kept bright in the weave
taboos: Wearing the wound instead of healing it
common_sayings: Tend the wound, do not wear it.
One root feels what the whole forest fears.
Grief is just growth that has not happened yet.
children_common_beliefs: A planted seed carries who you were
The rootwell only whispers to those who listen too long
class_differences: Grovekeepers revered for memory borne; sap-folk bear the harvest's risk
Border groves feel forgotten by the inner forest

religion.central_belief: Life is a cycle; what is patiently restored rejoins the weave, and what is harvested or commanded is torn from it.
common_prayers_or_oaths: Let me be a healthy root.
I return your name to the green.
heresies: The Rot Communion (corruption as a truer cycle)
The Frozen Grove (patience as the only virtue)
sacred_taboos: Wielding corrupted sap as a weapon
religion.relationship_to_death: Death is a return to the weave; a name kept bright is a death made whole.
religion.relationship_to_sacrifice: Sacrifice is the life-tithe to the cycle, not the spectacle of self-destruction.
religion.relationship_to_memory: Memory is the weave itself; to lose a name is the deepest death.
religion.relationship_to_truth: Truth must travel the roots; silencing it is a sacred wound.
religion.keeper_corruption_strategy: Promote the Rot Communion and the Frozen Grove as deeper faith.
religion.void_false_revelation_style: A green and gentle vision that the rot is simply the cycle the elders fear.

factions.name: Circle of Elders
factions.short_doctrine: Consensus stewardship of the cycle through the living weave.
factions.keeper_vulnerability: Frozen Patience and the Silencing Consensus.
factions.player_use: Lawful patron for patient, consensus-built paths.

factions.name: Rootwarden Conservators
factions.keeper_vulnerability: Split between cleansing ideals and Hollow Pact results.
factions.player_use: Allies for soul-flow healing and anti-corruption work.

factions.name: Communion Grovekeepers
factions.short_doctrine: Guard the weave's memory and render sacred judgment.
factions.power_base: Sacred arbitration and the network's truth.
factions.player_use: Arbiters, lore-source, and recoverers of lost names (Auralis).

factions.name: Sap Commons
factions.short_doctrine: Healing sap is a shared commons, not a monopoly.
factions.power_base: Economic control of sap and medicine.
factions.keeper_vulnerability: Sap famine pushing them toward corrupted supply.
factions.player_use: Source of healing, trade, and reform-minded allies.

factions.name: Bramble Thornguard
factions.short_doctrine: Endure and entangle; defend the groves without poisoning them.

factions.name: Hollow Pact
factions.short_doctrine: Survival justifies wielding the wound; the rot is a weapon, not a sin.
factions.keeper_vulnerability: Already a conduit for the rot it claims to master.
factions.player_use: Dangerous edge faction; recruiter of the desperate; tragic ally or antagonist (Nymara Hollowbloom).

npc_role_index.death_impact: The weave's truth dims; corrupted rootwells spread unspoken.

external_relations.hidden_relationship: Mutual dependency soured by fear of Radiance fire.
external_relations.primary_conflict: Radiance burns corruption Verdance would rather cleanse, sometimes without grove consent.
external_relations.primary_dependency: Verdance needs Radiance to hold the Abyss line; Radiance needs Verdance healing sap.
external_relations.resource_leverage: Verdance can embargo healing sap; Radiance can withhold frontier protection.
external_relations.magic_tension: Cycle versus fire; restoration versus purification.
external_relations.military_tension: Radiance haste clashes with Verdance patience at shared fronts.
external_relations.historical_wound: A grove burned without consent during a corruption scare.
external_relations.possible_alliance_condition: A shared Abyss soul-harvest threat on the border.
external_relations.keeper_exploit: Turn a containment burn into medical scarcity and mistrust.

external_relations.military_tension: Coordinating refugee corridors under Abyss pressure.

external_relations.possible_break_condition: Sanctuary gate closures stranding refugees in corrupted border zones.

external_relations.void_exploit: Offer the desperate a corrupted-sap shortcut to 'protect' their families.

external_relations.resource_leverage: Abyss studies corrupted-sap residue to engineer counter-corruption.
external_relations.magic_tension: Living memory versus name-harvest and soul-binding.

external_relations.possible_break_condition: Ceasefires shatter the moment names are harvested.
external_relations.keeper_exploit: Corner groves into wielding the rot, doing Abyss's work for it.
external_relations.void_exploit: Promise that mastering the rot can out-harvest the harvesters.

internal_power_struggles.title: The Thornveil Question
internal_power_struggles.issue: Whether Thornveil Refuge may use corrupted-sap traps to survive the Abyss siege.
internal_power_struggles.public_argument: Nymara: 'Cleansing is a luxury the dying cannot afford.' Thalen and the Conservators: 'A grove that wears the wound becomes it.'
internal_power_struggles.hidden_argument: Some wardens already tolerate the traps quietly; elders fear panic if the truth spreads through the weave.
possible_player_sides: Allow Hollow Pact traps to save the refuge now
internal_power_struggles.keeper_best_outcome: The traps stay, the soil rots, and the Hollow Pact's doctrine spreads.
internal_power_struggles.void_best_outcome: Corrupted-sap mastery becomes normalized along the border.
internal_power_struggles.peaceful_resolution: Supervised emergency use with mandatory cleansing and dismantling after the siege.
internal_power_struggles.violent_resolution: Conservators and Hollow Pact come to blows inside the besieged refuge.
internal_power_struggles.third_order_effect: Hollow Pact recruitment rises; Sap Commons reformers lose public trust.
internal_power_struggles.fifth_order_effect: The Keeper gains as Verdance's resistance damages its own soul-flow from within.

distrusted_sources: Anyone who left a grove to die
rumor_weaponization_methods: Branding cleansers as cowards who let villages die
rumor_mutation_patterns: 'Used corrupted sap to save them' becomes 'serves the rot'
A healer's mercy becomes 'touched a child's soul' then 'stole a child's soul'
A quarantine becomes 'the elders abandoned us'

trust_is_built_by: Cleansing a wound at personal cost
Returning a lost name to the weave
enemies_become_tolerable_when: They defend the weave against soul-harvest
They cleanse rather than command corruption
allies_become_suspect_when: They turn to corrupted shortcuts when afraid
romance_conflicts: A Hollow Pact lover who wields the rot the player opposes
A Radiance lover whose fire frightens the grove
betrayal_triggers: A silenced warning that gets people killed
forgiveness_conditions: Bearing the life-tithe to cleanse what one harmed

if_then_because_examples.if: The player weaponizes corrupted sap after promising cleansing
if_then_because_examples.then: Rootwarden trust falls and Hollow Pact interest rises
if_then_because_examples.because: Verdance distinguishes restoration from becoming the wound.

if_then_because_examples.if: A former enemy cleanses a corrupted rootwell at real cost
if_then_because_examples.then: Verdance may downgrade them from enemy to uneasy partner
if_then_because_examples.because: Tending the weave proves intent more deeply than past allegiance.

if_then_because_examples.if: The player returns a name the weave had lost
if_then_because_examples.because: A recovered name is the deepest restoration Verdance knows.

if_then_because_examples.if: An elder silences a true communion warning
if_then_because_examples.then: Border groves' trust in the Circle collapses once it surfaces
if_then_because_examples.because: Silencing the weave is a sacred wound to communion.

if_then_because_examples.if: The player saves a refuge using corrupted sap instead of cleansing
if_then_because_examples.then: Verdance respects the result but suspects the method
if_then_because_examples.because: To them, commanding the wound looks like surrendering the cycle to it.

if_then_because_examples.if: A healer uses forbidden soul-magic to save a child
if_then_because_examples.then: Verdance feels gratitude and fear together (trust and suspicion both rise)
if_then_because_examples.because: Life preserved but clean soul-passage violated is a genuine moral knot, not a simple win.

if_then_because_examples.if: A grove poisons its own soil to deny it to Abyss
if_then_because_examples.then: Conservators and elders condemn it even in victory
if_then_because_examples.because: Stewardship forbids destroying the cycle to win a season.

if_then_because_examples.if: The player exposes wardens quietly tolerating Hollow Pact traps
if_then_because_examples.then: Conservator respect rises but refuge morale drops
if_then_because_examples.because: Truth must travel the roots, even when it frightens the desperate.

if_then_because_examples.if: Abyss begins harvesting souls from Verdance border villages
if_then_because_examples.then: Rootwardens tolerate Hollow Pact ambushes for one mission
if_then_because_examples.because: Abyss ownership of Verdance souls is a greater violation than temporary cooperation with extremists.

if_then_because_examples.if: The player submits a hard choice to communion judgment
if_then_because_examples.then: Verdance factions grant more latitude on the outcome
if_then_because_examples.because: Communion shares the weight of the decision and the blame.

if_then_because_examples.if: A Radiance ally cleanses rather than burns a corrupted grove
if_then_because_examples.then: Verdance suspicion of Radiance fire eases into conditional trust
if_then_because_examples.because: Honoring the cycle over haste is the trust Verdance most wants to see.

cause_effect_examples.root_event: The player uses corrupted-sap traps to stop an Abyss patrol attacking Thornveil Refuge.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Verdance sees the refuge defended by weaponizing the wound instead of cleansing it.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: Nymara Hollowbloom praises the player; Thalen Mossguard demands an explanation; refugees argue over survival versus corruption.
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: The patrol is defeated and the refuge survives.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Hollow Pact respect +12; Rootwarden suspicion +10; soil corruption +4.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: Refugees split; Conservators open an inquiry; the rootwell stirs.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: Hollow Pact recruitment increases; Sap Commons reformers lose some public trust; a rumor spreads that Rootwardens secretly rely on corruption when afraid.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: Rootwarden authority weakens; Hollow Pact cells gain shelter in desperate villages; Abyss studies the trap residue to engineer counter-corruption.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: The Keeper benefits because Verdance's resistance begins damaging its own soul-flow from within.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: A conduit for the rot opens inside Verdance's defenses.
cause_effect_examples.void_gain: The Void whispers, 'If rot saved them, why call it corruption?'
player_intervention_options: Cleanse the trap residue
Publicly name the tactic emergency-only
Force Hollow Pact to dismantle the traps after the battle
Seek Auralis's communion judgment
Create a safer Sap Commons alternative

cause_effect_examples.root_event: The player uses forbidden soulbinding to save Elder Maera's dying son.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Verdance is torn: life preserved, but clean soul-passage through the weave violated.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: Communion Grovekeepers are alarmed; the Sap Commons are grateful; Hollow Pact sees a kindred willingness to break taboo.
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: The child survives, with a soul-scar.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Maera trust +8, fear +12, debt +20, suspicion +6; soul-flow integrity -2.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: Maera hides the child; word of the method reaches the Conservators.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: A rumor mutates from 'touched the child's soul' toward 'stole a child's soul.'
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: Conservators demand a cleansing review; a corrupted rootwell tugs at the scarred child.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: If unhealed, the scar becomes a new soul-flow wound the Keeper can exploit.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: A soul-scar that loosens a strand of the weave.
player_intervention_options: Seek a clean soul-healing method
Submit to communion judgment
Protect the child from the rootwell's pull
Counter the mutating rumor with the truth
Help Maera face the Conservators honestly

cause_effect_examples.root_event: The player uncovers and exposes a communion-finding the elders silenced about an accelerating border wound.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Verdance is forced to choose between trust in the elders and the duty of the weave to carry truth.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: Communion Grovekeepers are vindicated; complicit elders are shamed; border groves feel betrayed.
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: The finding spreads through the roots.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Circle of Elders legitimacy -10; border-grove trust in the player +12.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: A complicit elder resigns or retaliates; the Conservators mobilize toward the wound.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: Resources finally flow to the border, but a season late; reformers gain ground.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: The wound is contained at higher cost than early action would have required.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: The Keeper's Frozen-Patience and Silencing exploits are blunted, denying it a quiet victory.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: Reduced — unless the elders' fracture spirals into wider distrust.
player_intervention_options: Offer the elders a face-saving path to act
Protect the original whistleblower grove
Lead the delayed cleansing yourself
Mediate between reformers and traditionalists

cause_effect_examples.root_event: Abyss begins openly harvesting souls from three Verdance border villages.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Verdance treats name-harvest as the ultimate violation of the weave, overriding normal caution.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: Rootwardens and Hollow Pact find common cause; the Circle debates breaking its own taboos; the Sap Commons fear the front.
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: Names begin going silent in the weave.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Verdance soul-flow integrity -6; Rootwarden–Hollow Pact toleration forms for one mission.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: Conservators ambush the harvesters using Hollow Pact tactics they would normally forbid.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: The uneasy partnership wins ground but normalizes corrupted-sap use; recruitment rises.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: Some harvested names are recovered; others are lost; Abyss adapts its engines.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: Whether the Keeper gains depends on whether the toleration is ended and the rot cleansed afterward.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: Conditional: large if the Hollow Pact alliance becomes permanent, small if it is dissolved and cleansed.
player_intervention_options: Recover harvested names from the engines
Set a hard limit and breaking point on the Hollow Pact toleration
Lead the post-battle cleansing
Bring Auralis to re-weave the silenced strands
Expose Abyss debt-contracts coercing the survivors

cause_effect_examples.root_event: Facing a sap famine, the Circle of Elders counsels patience while a healable rootwell wound spreads beneath Thornveil.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Verdance's reverence for patience collides with the reality of an accelerating wound.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: Traditionalist elders urge waiting; reformers and Conservators demand action; the Hollow Pact offers corrupted sap as a 'solution.'
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: Aid is delayed as deliberation continues.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Rootwell Awakening clock +1; refugee morale -5; reformers' frustration rises.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: Healers are overruled by 'patience'; some refugees accept Hollow Pact help in secret.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: The rootwell wakes further, whispering stolen names; a rumor spreads that the elders abandoned the border.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: The wound that could have been cleansed in a day now requires a costly containment.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: The Keeper gains as Frozen Patience hands the rot exactly what it needed: time.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: Time for the corrupted rootwell to become unstoppable.
player_intervention_options: Force an emergency vote in communion
Cleanse the rootwell before it fully wakes
Rally reformers and Conservators to act without consensus
Discredit the Hollow Pact's 'solution' before it takes root
Find an emergency clean-sap source to relieve the famine

metaphysical: Can a name fully harvested by Abyss ever be returned to the weave, or only mourned?
Is a corrupted rootwell a wound to heal or a new, hostile node of the network?
political: Can consensus governance survive threats that move faster than the weave can deliberate?
How much emergency power can the Circle take before it stops being Verdance?
magic: Is there any safe, bounded use of corrupted sap, or is all rot-mastery a slope?
What exactly is given when a name is 'returned' to the weave?
faction: Is the Hollow Pact redeemable, or has the rot already mastered it?
How deep does the Silencing Consensus run in the Circle?
npc: Can Nymara Hollowbloom be turned from rot-mastery back to cleansing?
Does Elder Maera's debt make her an ally or a liability under pressure?
war_economy: How long can the Sap Commons feed both refugees and exports before collapse?
What happens to Verdance if the border groves fall and their names are harvested?
implementation: Should rot-debt be a corruption stat, a Void temptation event, or a soul-flow wound — or all three linked?
How are 'named seeds' modeled — as relics, as memory records, or as NPC links?

locked_decisions: Verdance magic must always involve the cycle, consent, restoration, or living memory.
Verdance corruption must distort restoration into rot-mastery and patience into stagnation, never become generic darkness.
Verdance internal politics must respect the Rootwarden / Hollow Pact / Sap Commons / Communion fracture.
Harvesting or silencing names in the weave is the violation Verdance cannot forgive.
Corrupted sap can grant real power, but every use deepens the soul-flow wound it came from.
Restoration is the cleansing of a wound; wearing or commanding the wound is its corruption.
